mechanism_narrative: The recent rebound in WORKPLACES and TRANSIT signals increasing weekday circulation that should lift discretionary shopping visits. If this recovery persists, RETAIL_REC should be higher over the next four weeks than over the last four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES improved from -28.6 to -17.7 and TRANSIT improved from -56.9 to -49.7 over the snapshot
failure_condition: If WORKPLACES and TRANSIT continue improving for two more weeks but RETAIL_REC remains below its prior 4-week mean, reject the hypothesis.

mechanism_narrative: Rising RESIDENTIAL mobility above 6% indicates more time spent at home, which suppresses in-store discretionary visits and pushes RETAIL_REC lower within two weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL stayed positive but fell from 10.1 to 6.1 over the snapshot
failure_condition: If RESIDENTIAL stays at or above its current level while RETAIL_REC rises over the next 14 days, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: A threshold break in TRANSIT matters: once TRANSIT improves by more than 5 points week-on-week from an already depressed level, shopping accessibility strengthens and RETAIL_REC turns up over the following four weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT rises > 5 points week-on-week from a level below -50
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT moved from -56.9 to -49.7 across the snapshot
failure_condition: If TRANSIT crosses above the threshold but RETAIL_REC does not increase relative to the last four weeks within 28 days, reject the hypothesis.

mechanism_narrative: When PARKS improve while WORKPLACES remain weak, leisure substitution can keep consumers near outdoor activities instead of retail venues, so RETAIL_REC falls over the next week.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS and WORKPLACES both remained negative, but PARKS were less depressed than WORKPLACES in the snapshot
failure_condition: If PARKS strengthen relative to WORKPLACES but RETAIL_REC does not weaken within 7 days, the interaction claim is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: Under tightening restrictions, weak TRANSIT combined with weak WORKPLACES reduces trip chaining and discretionary errands, causing RETAIL_REC to stay lower over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT remained near -50 and WORKPLACES near -18 in the latest week
failure_condition: If restrictions tighten but RETAIL_REC rises while both TRANSIT and WORKPLACES stay depressed, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: A late-winter softness in PARKS and RETAIL_REC can move together; if PARKS continue falling from already negative levels, retail outings usually soften with a two-week lag.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS declined from -8.1 to -14.0 over the snapshot
failure_condition: If PARKS keep declining but RETAIL_REC holds steady or rises over the next 14 days, reject the seasonal linkage.

mechanism_narrative: When GROCERY_PHARM is stable near baseline and RESIDENTIAL eases downward, household stock-up and stay-home pressure fade, freeing discretionary trips and lifting RETAIL_REC within four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM stayed near zero while RESIDENTIAL eased from 10.1 to 6.1
failure_condition: If GROCERY_PHARM remains near zero and RESIDENTIAL declines further but RETAIL_REC still weakens over 28 days, the hypothesis is false.

mechanism_narrative: If WORKPLACES improves for two consecutive weeks from its current depressed level, the commuting recovery will spill into nearby shopping trips and raise RETAIL_REC over the following month.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES rises for 2 consecutive weeks from below -15
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES improved from -26.9 to -17.7 over the snapshot
failure_condition: If WORKPLACES meets the trigger but RETAIL_REC does not exceed its prior 4-week mean within 28 days, reject the hypothesis.
